cards.topics: What is the Tabernacle, purpose, dwelling, tent of meeting
cards.answer: The Tabernacle was the portable sanctuary described in Exodus, built so that God would dwell among the Israelites. Its courtyard led into the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. Exodus 25:8–9.

cards.topics: Layout, rooms, directions, courtyard, entrance
cards.answer: The courtyard was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with its entrance on the east. The tent contained the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place, separated by a veil. Exodus 27:9–18 and 26:31–35.

cards.topics: Bronze altar, sacrifices, dimensions, fire, horns
cards.answer: The bronze altar stood in the courtyard. It was five cubits square and three cubits high, with a horn at each corner, made of acacia wood overlaid with bronze. Exodus 27:1–8.

cards.topics: Ashes, utensils, pots, shovel, forks, firepans, basins
cards.answer: The bronze altar utensils were pots for removing ashes, shovels, basins, forks and firepans. All were made of bronze. Exodus 27:3.

cards.topics: Washing basin, laver, mirrors, water, reflection, dimensions
cards.answer: The bronze basin and stand stood between the tent and altar, for the priests to wash their hands and feet. They were made from bronze mirrors. The text does not specify their dimensions. Exodus 30:17–21 and 38:8. Our water reflection is an educational reconstruction.

cards.topics: Menorah, lampstand, branches, candles, oil, wick
cards.answer: The gold lampstand had six side branches and a central stem, with seven lamps. They burned pure beaten olive oil, with wicks: Exodus 27:20–21 specifies the oil, and Exodus 25:38 lists wick trimmers and trays. These were oil lamps, rather than candles.

cards.topics: Almond cups, knobs, flowers, gold weight, one piece
cards.answer: The lampstand and its branches were hammered from pure gold, with almond-blossom cups, buds and flowers. Its lamps, wick trimmers and trays were gold. The lampstand and utensils used a talent of gold. Exodus 25:31–40.

cards.topics: Twelve loaves, showbread, bread, two stacks, frankincense, Sabbath
cards.answer: Twelve loaves were placed in two rows or arrangements of six on the pure gold table, with pure frankincense. They were renewed each Sabbath and eaten by Aaron and his sons in a holy place. Leviticus 24:5–9. Our two stacks are a reconstruction of that arrangement.

cards.topics: Bread table dimensions, dishes, bowls, pitchers, utensils
cards.answer: The table was two cubits long, one cubit wide and one and a half cubits high, of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Its gold utensils included dishes, pans or incense vessels, pitchers and bowls for pouring. Translations vary in the vessel names. Exodus 25:23–30.

cards.topics: Golden altar, incense altar, horns, tall square shape, location
cards.answer: The incense altar was one cubit square and two cubits high, with horns, made of acacia wood overlaid with gold. It stood before the veil. Aaron burned fragrant incense there morning and evening. Exodus 30:1–10. The text does not describe a separate ash plate on its top.

cards.topics: Incense recipe, fragrance, smoke, unauthorized incense
cards.answer: The sacred incense combined stacte, onycha, galbanum and pure frankincense in equal parts. It was reserved for holy use; the text forbids making the same mixture for personal fragrance. Exodus 30:34–38.

cards.topics: Veil, curtains, cherubim cloth, separation, entering most holy
cards.answer: The veil was made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it. It separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place. Exodus 26:31–35. Our tour permits educational access that was historically restricted.

cards.topics: Ark dimensions, wood, gold, poles, carrying
cards.answer: The ark was two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide and one and a half cubits high. It was acacia wood overlaid with gold inside and outside, with carrying rings and poles. Its poles were to remain in the rings. Exodus 25:10–16.

cards.topics: Cherubim, faces, wings, angels, mercy seat, ark cover
cards.answer: Two gold cherubim formed part of the ark cover, facing one another with their faces toward the cover and wings spread above it. Exodus 25:17–22 does not specify their detailed anatomy or facial style. Our sculpted figures and woven motifs are interpretive.

cards.topics: Ark contents, tablets, commandments, manna, Aaron staff
cards.answer: Exodus 25:16 instructs Moses to put the testimony in the ark. Exodus 16:33–34 describes preserved manna placed before the testimony; Numbers 17:10 places Aaron’s staff before it. Hebrews 9:4 later associates the manna, staff and covenant tablets with the ark. These passages describe different contexts.

cards.topics: High priest, who could enter, Day of Atonement, restricted access
cards.answer: Priests served in the Holy Place. Entry beyond the veil was restricted: Leviticus 16 describes Aaron entering with prescribed offerings and incense for atonement. Our Most Holy Place access is for education, not a reenactment of permission in ancient worship.

cards.topics: Aaron, priests, Levites, service
cards.answer: Aaron and his sons were appointed for priestly service, while the Levites had duties connected with caring for and transporting the sanctuary. Exodus 28:1 and Numbers 3–4 describe these responsibilities.

cards.topics: Priestly garments, ephod, breastpiece, robe, turban
cards.answer: Exodus 28 describes priestly garments including a breastpiece, ephod, robe, woven tunic, turban and sash. The visitor’s robe in this tour is an avatar costume, not a claim to be the high priest.

cards.topics: Bezalel, Oholiab, who built, craftsmanship
cards.answer: Bezalel and Oholiab were named for skilled work on the sanctuary, and willing-hearted craftspeople assisted. The materials came through offerings from the people. Exodus 31:1–11 and 35–36.

cards.topics: Materials, gold, silver, bronze, linen, wool, acacia, colors
cards.answer: The offerings included gold, silver, bronze, colored yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, skins, acacia wood, oil, spices and precious stones. Exodus 25:1–7. The tent’s exact appearance involves reconstruction choices beyond those written instructions.

cards.topics: Roof, coverings, skins, tent curtains, boards, sockets
cards.answer: Exodus 26 describes linen curtains with cherubim, goats’ hair curtains, protective skin coverings, acacia frames overlaid with gold, silver bases and connecting bars. The meaning of one covering-material term differs across translations.

cards.topics: Cubits, measurements, meters, scale, heights
cards.answer: A cubit is an ancient forearm-based unit whose exact length varied. Exodus gives the furnishings’ dimensions in cubits; converting them into modern meters requires choosing an approximate cubit length. The basin’s dimensions are not specified.

cards.topics: Travel, dismantle, carry, wilderness, poles, movement
cards.answer: The sanctuary was portable. Numbers 4 assigns transport duties and describes covering furnishings before carrying them. Its rings and poles supported transport; the ark’s poles remained in place. Exodus 25:12–15.

cards.topics: Moses, wilderness, Exodus, Sinai, completion, first erected
cards.answer: Exodus describes the Tabernacle instructions in the wilderness and its erection on the first day of the first month of the second year. The glory filled the sanctuary. Exodus 40:17 and 34–38. This tour depicts the Mosaic sanctuary, not Solomon’s later temple.

cards.topics: Viewing assistance, avatar, tablet, robot, controls, tour
cards.answer: Your left-hand tablet contains Instructions, Tour and Settings. Hold X on the left controller to ask a question after the welcome. Viewing assistance in Comfort settings raises your viewpoint temporarily; it does not change historical furniture dimensions.
